change.summary: Persist a changed automatic route through the private atomic routing-state boundary before updating the in-memory route or opening the selected upstream attempt.

test_first.command: timeout 30s node --test --test-name-pattern='does not contact an automatic route' packages/account-router/test/runtime-persistence.test.mjs

before_implementation.observed_failure: The fixture route store rejected its save, but the response was HTTP 200 from the fixture upstream instead of a pre-contact sanitized 502.
before_implementation.bounded_cleanup: The command exited normally in 89 milliseconds.

failure_injections: an automatic route save failure returns before any upstream contact
a successful automatic upstream attempt remains blocked until the private save gate is released
manual acknowledgement and semantic-race rollback remain unchanged

covers: HTTP/SSE bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
WebSocket bounded pre-semantic failover and post-semantic no-replay
durable automatic and manual routing boundaries

deployment.reason: The previously proven sudo root-GID transition failure and non-writable /opt/codex-account-router boundary are unchanged.

remaining_limits: 0.2.13 is verified but is not active until a host-privileged operator runs the rollback-capable router-only deployment script.

Persist-before-contact adds one local private atomic write only when the automatic route changes; this is fixture-covered but has not been measured on deployed 8216, so no production latency claim is made.
A private routing-state persistence failure makes automatic and manual route changes fail closed until an operator resolves the state boundary.
The tests use synthetic accounts only and do not qualify a real A-to-B switch.
Real two-account verification remains blocked until explicit enrollment authorization.
